scope: Published supplier inventory and missing proof designs for numerical ODE, nonlinear-solver, BVP, and geometric integration authoring.
inspection_note: Statements and proof sections below were inspected in current published carriers. Continuous or algebraic supplier claims are not treated as numerical-method theorems.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.title: First-order systems, initial value problems, and solutions on intervals
existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: Defines an IVP on an open time-state domain and a solution on an order-convex interval, including domain-relative endpoint derivatives.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.title: Picard-Lindelöf local existence and uniqueness for first-order systems
existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: Continuous locally state-Lipschitz field on an open domain gives a unique local solution. On a compact cylinder, ||F||<=M, state-Lipschitz constant L, hM<=r, and Lh<1 give exactly one solution staying in that cylinder.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.proof: Volterra equivalence, complete curve space, invariant ball, Banach contraction.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.limit: Does not prove discrete consistency, stability, or convergence.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: A Picard–Lindelöf IVP has a unique maximal solution on an open interval; all solutions through the data are restrictions.
For continuous F and curve on an order-convex interval, the IVP is equivalent to x(t)=x0+int_(t0)^t F(s,x(s)) ds, with oriented integrals.
Two solutions with a common state-Lipschitz bound L along their graphs obey ||x(t)-y(t)||<=exp(L|t-t0|)||x(t0)-y(t0)||.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.proof: Subtract Volterra equations and apply integral Grönwall.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.limit: Continuous-flow stability does not imply a numerical step-map Lipschitz estimate.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: Variable- and constant-coefficient integral Grönwall, with reflected-time forms.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.limit: No discrete Grönwall supplier is published.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: Nearby parameterized IVPs share a compact time interval and satisfy an explicit exponential estimate in initial time/state and parameter perturbations.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.proof: Compact-cylinder Picard–Lindelöf, uniform continuity, Volterra equations, integral Grönwall.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.limit: Supports shooting sensitivity context; numerical sensitivity error remains separate.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: A smooth nonautonomous field has a common local solution interval and smooth solution map in initial time and state.
For f in C^(k+1) on an open convex set, gives a Taylor polynomial and Lagrange remainder along a segment.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.limit: Only supplies remainders under its convex-segment and smoothness conditions; it does not establish a method order.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: A self-map contraction with factor q<1 on a nonempty complete metric space has a unique fixed point; iterates from any start converge with a geometric tail bound.
A priori and a posteriori fixed-point errors are bounded by q^n d(x1,x0)/(1-q) and q d(x_(n+1),x_n)/(1-q).
For f C^1 and Df(a) invertible, x+Df(a)^(-1)(y-f(x)) is a contraction on a small closed ball, uniformly in y; Df remains invertible there with a bound.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.proof: Bounds Df(x)-Df(a), applies the mean-value inequality, and uses Banach to show nearby derivatives invertible.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.limit: Jacobian is frozen at a. This is not convergence of the usual variable-Jacobian Newton iteration.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: A symplectic form is a smooth closed, pointwise nondegenerate two-form.
Symplectic means literal pullback equality F^*omega_N=omega_M; a symplectomorphism is also a diffeomorphism.
Library convention i_(X_H) omega=dH; completeness is not assumed.
H is constant on every integral curve of X_H on its connected maximal interval.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.proof: Differentiate H along the curve and use alternation of omega.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: Under AC_omega, each defined time slice of a time-dependent Hamiltonian evolution is a local symplectomorphism.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.proof: Differentiate the pulled-back form and use Cartan's formula.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.limit: Carry AC_omega and local-domain hypotheses if consumed.

existing_published_supplier_contracts.contract: Hamiltonian vector fields have zero divergence relative to symplectic volume.
existing_published_supplier_contracts.limit: Continuous volume preservation does not imply a numerical map preserves volume or the original energy.

missing_prerequisite_designs.proof_route: Use compact-tube Taylor bounds and direct step-map estimates, then consume P-NUM-ODE-01/02. Prove discrete Grönwall if used generically.
Prove characteristic-root condition including repeated roots, bound companion-system powers, then propagate O(h^(p+1)) residuals with O(h^p) starting values.
Compute test-equation stability factors. Prove backward Euler's L-limit; show A-stability alone is insufficient using trapezoidal rule.
Define accept/reject and controller rules. A global guarantee needs estimator reliability, mesh regularity, and global accumulation.
Taylor expansion around a regular root plus inverse-Jacobian bound and an invariant local basin; the frozen-Jacobian lemma is not a substitute.
Establish e_h=A_h^(-1)tau_h in a declared norm. For shooting, include the IVP sensitivity condition factor.
Reuse continuous Hamiltonian suppliers; construct only a finite modified equation and sum truncation defects on a compact orbit.

supplier_order_guidance: Use continuous ODE existence, stability, dependence, and Taylor suppliers only for their exact continuous claims.
Prove algebraic nonlinear-solver prerequisites before implicit IVP and BVP consumers.
Carry geometric suppliers' domain and choice assumptions; symplecticity is not exact energy conservation.
